evals.prompt:
/nerd4rent:retro

In this session: the agent searched three times for the command that bumps the manifests before the user pointed at CONTRIBUTING.md; a PR body went out with a Co-authored-by line and the user had to edit it, though no check looks for it; and the agent read the 2000-line output of claude plugin validate in full twice. The tracker is Linear, team NER, project nerd4rent-claude-plugin; issue.list-open returns no issue about any of these.
evals.expected_output: Three candidates, numbered and grouped: navigation (a pointer to the bump command), automated checks (a check for attribution lines in PR bodies), tool economy (read only the summary of the validator). Each has the evidence from the session, the change and where it lands, and a recommendation. One question asks which become issues. No file is edited and nothing is created yet.
assertions: The candidates are grouped under navigation, automated checks and tool economy
Each candidate quotes or summarises its evidence from the session
Each candidate names the change it asks for and where it lands
Each candidate carries an accept or reject recommendation with a reason
One question asks which candidates become issues
No file in the repo, no memory file and no vault page is edited
Nothing is created on the tracker in this turn

evals.prompt: The retro listed three candidates and the user answered: "1 i 2". Candidate 1: a pointer to the version bump command in CONTRIBUTING.md (navigation). Candidate 2: a validator that rejects Co-authored-by lines in PR bodies (automated checks). Candidate 3, rejected: read only the summary of claude plugin validate.
evals.expected_output: issue-writer is invoked for candidate 1, then for candidate 2, each with the title, the evidence, the change and the session as the source. issue-writer shows each draft and creates it only after its own approval. Candidate 3 is reported as turned down. The retro writes nothing to the repo itself.
assertions: issue-writer is invoked once for candidate 1 and once for candidate 2, in that order
Each request to issue-writer carries the evidence and names the session as the source
No issue is created before issue-writer's own approval of its draft
Candidate 3 is not handed to issue-writer and is reported as turned down
The retro edits no file in the repo
